features: NO DATABASE CHANGES — One topic: paying on someone else's behalf. The buyer who settles the seller's arrears, the son who pays his mother's instalment: the debt stays with whoever owes it, and whoever paid stays on record. This beta also brings in a principle that will guide the rest of the program: when there is more than one legitimate path and the right one depends on an agreement between people, the program does not choose silently, it asks the administrator. No migration: the link to whoever paid uses a field of the accounting lines that already existed. Changes of behaviour are listed first.

CHANGED: ONE FUND'S CREDIT ON ANOTHER FUND'S INSTALMENTS — When the credit of one fund would cover an instalment of another (ordinary-fund credit on the roof instalment), the form asks «Does the credit move to another fund?»: «Only on its own fund» or «On the other funds too». The question appears only when the answer changes the amounts, and without an answer the payment is not recorded. Before, the confirmation checkbox appeared only in some cases, and the server recorded the move anyway, with the note «confirmed by the administrator». This applies without «Paid by» too.

CHANGED: CREDIT ACROSS SEVERAL FUNDS, IN AUTOMATIC MODE — A fund's credit covers by itself only that fund's instalments, and the money paid in pays the instalments oldest first. Before, money and credit were spent together by due date, on any fund: an older instalment of another fund also took the credit. With a single fund nothing changes. Arriving from a link that already points to the instalment (a payment report, «Offset» from the account statement, the «Credits to offset» box), without «Paid by», the form works as before.

CHANGED: THE FUND OF THE PAYMENT — A payment covering instalments of several funds, with the «Fund» filter empty, asks which fund it goes to («Fund of the payment»). Before, the program took the fund of one of the instalments with no criterion, not always the one the form suggested. Instalments covered only by credit count too, because the fund is written on both the payment and the offset. With instalments of a single fund, that fund is used without asking.

«PAID BY» — In the new payment, under the person, there is the «Paid by» field: whoever actually made the transfer, when it is another person of the building. The payer stays whoever owes, and the money closes their instalments as always. The cash line says «on behalf of», the lines closing the debt say «paid by». It is chosen among the people of this building. Without money paid in it has no effect: an offset made only with credit has nobody paying.

THE DEBTOR'S CREDIT — If whoever owes has a credit, with «Paid by» the form asks what to do with it: «Stays with …» (the money paid in goes first, and the credit stays theirs) or «Use it now» (credit first, then the money paid in). It depends on what they agreed, so nothing is pre-selected, and until the choice is made «Confirm payment» stays disabled with the reason written next to it.

THE EXTRA AMOUNT — If whoever paid sends more than the debt, the extra goes to them, not to the debtor: on one of their issued instalments in this building, reducing it or becoming their credit. The form proposes the first unpaid one in the fund of the payment; an instalment of another fund can be chosen, and the form warns that the extra moves to that fund. If whoever paid has no issued instalments here, the extra is not recorded: only the debt is recorded and the difference is returned.

WHERE IT SHOWS — The list and the detail of payments say who paid, and the search finds them by name. The debtor's account statement carries the note on the line; the payer's has a «Payments on behalf of others» box, on screen and in the PDF, which does not touch their balance. In the Journal («Prima nota») and in the ledgers the counterparty is «whoever paid on behalf of whoever owes». Reversing such a payment also cancels the extra amount, and the box marks it as reversed. If that extra had already been used as credit, the reversal brings back a debt without warning, as has always happened to the payer: the warning is queued.

FIXED: THE PAYMENT CHECK OF AN INSTALMENT — The «Payment check» task of an instalment closed when the sum of payments reached the total: one owner's advance payment hid another owner's debt. Now it closes only when every share of the instalment is paid, and a reversal reopens it only if the instalment is no longer settled.

FIXED: HAND-CRAFTED REQUESTS — When saving a payment, a person id sent as a list became person no. 1, even of another building; for cash account, fund and instalments it gave an error page. Now it is a validation error. The task closed by a payment coming from a payment report must belong to this building: before, one of another building could be closed.
A PERSON WHO PAID FOR SOMEONE ELSE CANNOT BE DELETED — As long as a payment names them in «Paid by», their record stays: deleting it would remove from the register who paid.

THE GUIDE — In the new-payment guide, the section «Who paid for someone else» explains the two choices, and the «Credit» tab says when credit is included by itself: with «Use it now», and arriving without «Paid by» from a link that already points to the instalment (the credit of that instalment's fund).

NOT YET — A distribution table where the administrator sees and changes, instalment by instalment, how much the credit pays and how much the money, with the possible paths offered as proposals: it comes in a dedicated beta. Until then the choices are the ones described above.

FOR DEVELOPERS — Which credit goes on which instalment is decided by a single function, PianoCreditoIncasso, which has a mirror in the form (pianoCreditoIncasso.ts) and a shared table of cases (tests/Fixtures/piano_credito_incasso.json): if the two stop computing the same, a test turns red. Payment and reversal update the schedule from the same instalment-person pairs (EventiRataCondomino).
